question: Ticket 7dcecacd7809 says "Clause 1 of the falsifier: 'unhelped_sites over skills/sail names no file' verifies that every subprocess call in sweep.py takes helper keywords. Decision D1 claims 'every subprocess call in sweep.py takes the helper's keywords.'", but outline 9.4.2.3.6 reads "Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git)." (The ticket's why explicitly states 'the scan that guards the helper looks only for Popen,' but the ticket claims to fix 'every subprocess call' (documented measurement checked run, Popen, call, check_output, check_call). The proof cannot verify what it doesn't measure: if sweep.py contains unhelped subprocess.run() or subprocess.call() without marker comments, the Popen-only scanner leaves them undetected. This violates 9.4.2.3.6: the tooth must measure the right thing, and if it only checks one method while claiming to verify all methods, it measures incompletely. Either the code (sweep.py) must only use Popen, or the proof's falsifier clause 1 must be tightened to reflect what unhelped_sites actually verifies.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
